title: ADR: Telemetry aggregation, retention hierarchy, and cost partitioning
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This ADR records the decision to adopt a hierarchical telemetry aggregation and retention model for Redwood Inference. The model balances developer and SRE needs for high-fidelity observability with long-term cost constraints by defining three telemetry tiers (hot, warm, cold), a clear retention schedule, in-ingest aggregation rules, and a cost-partitioning methodology that maps observability spend to product teams and customers.

Motivation:

- Observability costs have grown 3.8x year-over-year driven by uncurated high-cardinality metrics and full-fidelity traces for every request.
- Teams need predictable SLIs and the ability to debug production incidents with sufficient granularity.
- Finance requires transparent allocation of telemetry spend for chargeback and budgeting.

Goals:

1) Ensure page/actionable alerts remain supported by high-fidelity telemetry for the top 1% of traffic (latency-sensitive flows) for 14 days.
2) Preserve medium-fidelity traces and downsampled metrics for engineering troubleshooting for 90 days.
3) Keep long-term aggregated indicators (p95/p99/throughput) for 13 months for trend analysis and capacity planning.
4) Provide a deterministic cost-partitioning mechanism that attributes ingestion and storage costs to the correct owning team and billing account.

Decision:

We will implement a hierarchical telemetry system with the following components and rules: 

- Telemetry tiers:
  - Hot (raw, high-cardinality): Sampled full-resolution metrics/traces for high-priority services and requests. Retention: 14 days.
  - Warm (downsampled/aggregated): 1m/5m aggregated metrics and sampled trace spans for medium priority. Retention: 90 days.
  - Cold (rollups/aggregates): Daily rollups, retention: 13 months, stored in cost-efficient object store and queryable via analytical pipeline.

- Ingest-time policies:
  - Every telemetry event is assigned a telemetry_tier label during ingestion by the otel-collector pipeline based on request attributes and routing rules.
  - Default policy: services marked as latency-sensitive in the Service Registry (see table below) get Hot for 5% of traffic, Warm for 25%, Cold for the rest.
  - Manual overrides: On-call or Release Managers can temporarily elevate a service to higher sampling for incident windows using the Observability Control API.

- Aggregation rules:
  - Counter metrics: roll up using sum; gauges: preserve max/min/avg + sum/count for derivation.
  - High-cardinality labels (user_id, prompt_hash) are stripped at Hot->Warm boundary unless explicitly whitelisted.
  - Canonical dimensions to keep: service_name, model_variant, region, route_id, error_class.

- Trace sampling:
  - Head-based sampler with probabilistic sampling of 5% default across all services.
  - Priority sampling for traces that exceed an alerting threshold (error >= 5% or latency > SLA) — these are always captured as Hot for 72 hours following the event.
  - Retain full span payload for Hot traces; retain span metadata only for Warm traces (span ids, duration, tags).

- Cost partitioning:
  - Attach telemetry_cost_center metadata on ingest derived from service ownership metadata in the Service Registry.
  - Storage and ingestion costs are calculated per telemetry_cost_center using daily partitioned billing exports from the telemetry backend.
  - Allocation rules: 70% direct (usage by cost_center), 20% shared infra (distributed by service request volume), 10% central platform (observability platform team).

Service registry sample (fields used by telemetry pipeline):

| service_name | owner_team | latency_sensitive | default_sample_rate | cost_center |
|--------------|------------|-------------------:|---------------------:|-------------|
| edge-proxy   | eng-platform | true              | 0.05                | platform    |
| serving-runtime | eng-serving-runtime | true     | 0.05                | runtime     |
| kv-cache-coordinator | eng-serving-runtime | false | 0.01              | runtime     |
| billing-worker | finance-legal | false           | 0.005               | billing     |

Operational implications and SLOs:

- SLI preservation: For every production alert we must confirm Hot-tier telemetry exists for the affected service and time window for at least 14 days. Failure to provide results in an observability SLO breach.
- Ingest latency: Telemetry write path must not add more than 25ms median per-event overhead.
- Data access: Engineers must be able to retrieve raw Hot traces for the 14-day window via the Observability Console with RBAC.

Rollout plan (high level):

1) Week 0-2: Deploy telemetry_tier annotation pipeline in staging; run shadow classification against last 30 days of synthetic/staging traffic.
2) Week 3-4: Pilot with two services (edge-proxy, serving-runtime). Collect cost and utility metrics.
3) Week 5-6: Expand to all critical services (top 20 by request volume). Enable cost export integration.
4) Week 7-10: Full rollout to production with retros and SLO tracking.

Migration steps for historical data:

1) Run batch aggregation of last 90 days into Warm rollups (1m aggregates).
2) Generate daily rollups for 13 months and place them into long-term cold storage (S3/BigQuery export).
3) Retain raw hot-indexed traces for only 14 days before deletion.

Examples and sample queries:

- PromQL (1m warm aggregate CPU use by service):
  sum by (service_name) (rate(service_cpu_seconds_total[1m]))

- Example cost attribution SQL (pseudo):
  SELECT cost_center, SUM(storage_cost + ingestion_cost) AS total_cost
  FROM telemetry_billing_export
  WHERE date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE
  GROUP BY cost_center

- Example log/metric tag enforcement (ingest policy rule):
  - If telemetry.source == "edge-proxy" AND response_code >= 500 THEN telemetry_tier = "Hot"; force_capture = true

Alternatives considered:

- Keep full-resolution telemetry for all services indefinitely: rejected due to linear growth in cost and degraded query performance.
- Aggressive uniform sampling (e.g., 0.5% for everything): rejected because it jeopardizes incident debugging and SLO root-cause analysis.
- Store raw traces in cold object store with on-demand rehydration: considered but rejected for now due to rehydration latency (hours) that would harm time-to-resolution.

Security, privacy and compliance considerations:

- High-cardinality PII (user_id, email, prompt_content) must be redacted before Hot storage unless whitelisted by data-privacy review.
- Telemetry pipelines must maintain encryption-in-transit and at-rest. KMS-managed keys are mandatory for Cold storage.

Monitoring and alerting changes:

- New observability SLO: "Hot-availability" — percentage of alerts for which Hot telemetry exists for the incident window. Target: 99.0% monthly.
- Cost spikes: alert when daily telemetry ingestion cost exceeds 120% of the 30-day moving average. Primary contacts: observability@redwood.com, eng-sre pager.

Ownership and governance:

- Observability platform team owns the pipeline and enforcement rules.
- Service teams maintain the Service Registry entries and the cost_center mapping.
- Finance reviews monthly billing exports and approves chargeback allocations.

Open questions and future work:

- Evaluate selective on-demand rehydration for critical traces to reduce cold-storage rehydration latency.
- Explore ML-backed anomaly detection to elevate sampling dynamically for unusual behavior.

Appendix: checkout checklist for release engineers (copyable):

1) Ensure service has owner and cost_center set in Service Registry.
2) Verify default_sample_rate and latency_sensitive flags are correct.
3) Run staging shadow classification and confirm telemetry_tier assignment matches expectations.
4) Confirm KMS keys and export pipeline to cold storage are healthy.
5) Verify cost_export integration to finance pipeline is receiving records.

References:

- Observability ingestion design doc (internal): /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/telemetry-ingestion-and-retention-guidelines-2025
- Service Registry spec: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/service-registry-spec

Sign-off:

This ADR was approved by the Observability Working Group and signed off by the engineering leadership group on 2026-01-29.

Decision: Adopt hierarchical telemetry aggregation, retention tiers, and cost partitioning as described above.
